note: Attacker-controlled bytes are copied into a mutable buffer and become the configuration input for parsing.
The fuzzer input length is reduced by one and passed into the config parser as the mapped input range.
The lexer is initialized to scan the attacker-controlled buffer from start to end.
A leading quote sequence routes the lexer into multiline-string handling, which inspects bytes ahead of the current position.
The lexer chooses the closing delimiter based on the next attacker-controlled byte and then scans forward for that delimiter.
The sink is a 3-byte read from the current lexer position; if the input ends near the delimiter check, strncmp reads past the mapped buffer and triggers the global-buffer-overflow.
